title: the-tester-is-reached-only-through-its-interface
intention: Nothing outside the tester device reaches into its code: the tester answers a `run` bus verb (one proof, sink none, the record back as JSON) that cairn/tools/base/validation.run_proof and every foreign proof that runs a proof through TesterDevice ask instead; proof discovery (cairn/devices/tester/discovery.py, standard library only) moves down a rung to a tool; and the foreign teeth that measure tester internals (cli flag folding, hollow._buildme_at and hollow.measure, the scratch-sweep seal refusal, codemother's seal-by-run) move into the tester's own proofs, so each component's proofs measure only that component.
why: RULE 1 child: 15 encapsulation rows reach into the tester beyond its store; the bus and the tester's own proofs are the declared paths
traces_to: RULE 1 (a device's public interface is the bus; a ticket's proofs measure only its component; contracts are proved on both sides) via parent 8e3474a6ae43; Law 8 (the run verb carries the tester's verdict, read not granted).
how: Measured 2026-10-02 (encapsulation_breaches('.') in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py): 15 rows into the tester other than its store — cairn.devices.tester.device 7 (cairn/tools/base/validation.py:100, proofs in harbor_master, codemother x2, db_domain, proof_coverage), cli 3 (codemother constrain proof, system_word proof and probe), hollow 3 (cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_crossings_are_derived.py x2, cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_call_time_binding.py), scratch_sweep 1 (db_domain proof), discovery 1 (cairn/tools/base/validation.py:35). The device-path pattern exists: a device declares declared_verbs() and the shim posts the handler's dict back as the reply (cairn/tools/base/shim.py), callers use bus_client.reach(name).request(...) (cairn/web_server/listener.py asks trouble 'live' that way). The bus rides the Postgres Unix socket (cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py SOCKET_DIR), which crosses a network namespace, so a netns-sealed proof can ask it.
falsifier: RED if: (1) the live encapsulation_breaches('.') carries any row whose module starts with cairn.devices.tester; (2) the tester's declared_verbs() has no `run`, or a `run` request over the bus for a green fixture proof returns a record whose verdict is not green, or for a red one not red; (3) cairn/tools/base/validation.py imports anything from cairn.devices. WRONG INTENT if a foreign proof's tooth cannot be expressed either over the bus or as a tester-side tooth without losing what it measured. Horizon: the tester seal of the new proof.
watchme: none, because the encapsulation_holds sieve in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py reds any new reach into the tester at the next inspect, and the run verb is exercised by every proof that asks it
children: none, because the verb, the discovery move and the teeth relocation are one boundary closed in one build
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/devices/tester/device.py declared_verbs gains 'run'; cairn/tools/base/validation.py run_proof asks it; discovery.py moves to a tool; foreign teeth move into cairn/devices/tester/proofs/. (2) What? see the intention; each foreign site is listed in the how. (3) Proof? a new tester proof with PROVES keys 1, 2, 3, red first.

decisions.text: cairn/devices/tester/device.py, class TesterDevice: add declared_verbs(self) returning {**super().declared_verbs(), 'run': self._handle_run}; add _handle_run(self, envelope) that reads body=envelope.get('body') or {}, path=str(body.get('path') or ''); if not os.path.isfile(path) return {'refused': 'no proof file at <path> — nothing was run and no verdict was read'}; else return {'record': self.run_proof(path, sink='none', caller=str(body.get('caller') or envelope.get('sender') or 'unknown'), timeout=int(body.get('timeout') or 120))}. run_proof itself is unchanged (it already takes caller and timeout); the record is the standard eight-field VALIDATION it returns.

git mv cairn/devices/tester/discovery.py cairn/tools/proof_discovery/proof_discovery.py (body unchanged; REPO_ROOT = parents[3] holds at the new depth; docstring names its new address), add an empty cairn/tools/proof_discovery/__init__.py, a charter cairn/tools/proof_discovery/intention+why.json (runtime_role tool, public_interface ['cairn.tools.proof_discovery.proof_discovery']), and cairn/tools/proof_discovery/proofs/test_proof_discovery.py (a proofs/ dir and a directory containing one are both expanded; a missing path is kept and printed). cairn/devices/tester/cli.py:74 becomes 'from cairn.tools.proof_discovery.proof_discovery import REPO_ROOT, discover'. cairn/tools/base/validation.py discover() imports 'from cairn.tools.proof_discovery.proof_discovery import discover as _discover'; validation.run_proof is deleted.

The proof_discovery charter copies the field set of cairn/tools/validation_store/intention+why.json (component, runtime_role 'tool', role 'charter', schema_version, node_class 'tool', public_interface ['cairn.tools.proof_discovery.proof_discovery'], what, why, entry 'GRAFTED by git mv from cairn/devices/tester/discovery.py, ticket 67b78ae59c1d', invoke, state_and_history, proof, gates, falsifier, learns, how_it_learns, traces_to, owner, gated_by, claim_provenance), written through `cairn charter` / the artifact door. test_proof_discovery.py asserts over a scratch tree: (1) discover([<dir>/proofs]) returns that dir's test_*.py files; (2) discover([<dir>]) returns every <dir>/**/proofs/test_*.py, sorted and deduped; (3) discover([<missing>]) returns [Path(<missing>)] and prints 'cairn test: no such path: <missing>' to stderr.

In constrain._run_instrument after the bus ask: record = body.get('record'); if not isinstance(record, dict): state = {'verdict': 'unrunnable', 'how': body.get('refused') or 'the tester returned no record'}; else state = {'verdict': record.get('verdict'), 'how': 'run by the tester'}.
